question: Add a limits[].kind and binding term for a compute-time pool (minutes, credits or vCPU-minutes a month, or a count of builds a month), for example compute-quota, defined as an allowance of compute time or credits over a period, counted per account?
why: The seven-term vocabulary has no term for it. The dossier README defines volume-quota as a byte allowance, and request-rate as calls per unit time, so a monthly compute pool fits neither, and the corpus files it both ways: in ci-cd-runners, request-rate holds 7 pools (azure-pipelines-private 1,800 minutes, circleci-free 30,000 credits, cirrus-ci 50 credits, cloudflare-workers-builds 3,000 minutes, garnix 1,500 minutes, github-actions-private, gitlab-ci 400 compute minutes, harness-ci-free 2,000 credits, semaphore-cloud USD 15 of credit) while buildkite-free files 2,000 vCPU-minutes as volume-quota; compute/buildkite is volume-quota and compute/buildkite-hosted request-rate for the same 2,000 vCPU-minutes. compute/buddy files a USD 1 monthly credit as per-object-cap. The kind is also the binding term, so a CI record whose pool binds must name request-rate, which METHODOLOGY section 4.3 says bounds calls. Across compute, request-rate and volume-quota hold dozens of minute, credit and core-hour pools (for example compute/azure-pipelines, compute/bitbucket-pipelines, compute/cloudflare-containers, compute/aws-free-plan-t4g). Until the term exists, a lane files a pool under request-rate and names the true term in binding_note.
